questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: UC Berkely is a renowned university with high academic standards and some of the best professors in the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot information to gather but I think the meetings (and particularly the slideshow from the meetings) were very helpful and informative. However, it would be convenient with one document in which all information you need for the specific UC campus is gathered because it is still very widespread where to find some specific information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was welcomed to the university by some guides for new students and exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The UCEAP reciprocity website is very helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university offered a lot of different on campus housing options. I lived at a place called International House which is not facilitated through the university but is still an on-campus housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In most on campus housing options meal plans are included.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very convenient with meal plans and short distance to classes, however, it is also very expensive and you could save a lot money by looking at off campus options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before you attend the university, you get a time slot from which you can make an early registration for courses. It is a good idea to enroll in the courses in the early registration phase, as some of the popular courses are quickly full. After that, when you arrive at Berkeley the first couple of weeks are a so-called "add and drop period" where you can attend different classes and are able to switch courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A detailed description of the course registration schedule can be found at the university's website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was somewhat succesful. I got most of the course that I wanted to, however, there was one course that I didn't get, which is because full-time students get earlier access for the early registration phase than exchange students, thus the cornerstone courses can be hard to register for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Exploit the add and drop period and attend a lot of different classes in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I both took undergraduate and graduate courses. I was at my first semester of my master's when I attended Berkeley, and I would say that the graduate courses were at a very high level (and extremely insightful) and can probably be compared to PhD courses at the UCPH, while the level of the undergraduate are in general quite low (even though you can find courses that are still at an advanced level on the undergrad).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were a much larger focus on recent findings in research and explaining the economic trends, while the style of teaching at UCPH is much more textbook based.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Graduate Public Economics, Global Inequality and Growth, Topics in Economic Research, Econometrics: Advanced Methods and Applications.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Public Economics at the graduate level with Emmanuel Saez and Mathilde Munoz is probably the most exciting and inspiring course I have through my entire time of studying. You learned very much and directly from the research frontier. I can highly recommend that course.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was very expensive. I knew before that it was expensive but considering what you get for the amount of moeny you pay then it was crazy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost all the types of sports you can imagine are available for students for free or for a very low expense.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a part of a soccer club where we participated in a tournament against other teams of Berkeley students. I can very much recommend doing that sort of social activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I very much enjoyed just spending time on campus and maybe going to San Francisco once in a while. For me the purpose of the exchange stay was not to explore the entire California, but on the other hand to try to get the sense of what it means to be a UC Berkeley student and to live like a local. Therefore, I didn't travel that much around but enjoyed my weekends in Berkeley/SF.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports club or live at residence halls or co-ops.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pride and identity associated with being a student of a top university.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be well-prepared before you go such that you can get the most out of your time while you are there. 
2. Try not to live at an apartment or anything similar because living with many other people is a great part of the experience and you potentially get a huge international network and learn many things about other countries and cultures. If you want to save money look at co-ops instead of apartments.
3. Enjoy your time and try to be engaged in the UC Berkeley community by joining sports clubs, going to social events, and being active in your courses (e.g., it is a great opportunity that you are able to go office hours)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing social life and academics.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
